sourceAttempts.notes: Used to freeze prior decisions and identify names. No local statement was treated as formal evidence.
CVF, NeurIPS, AAAI, IEEE DOI, AAMAS DOI, MDPI DOI, and IET DOI pages were preferred where a formal version exists.
Retained alongside the formal link when both exist; used as the primary record only for preprints without a verified formal destination.
Used for released demos, tables, dataset indexes, and exact code/checkpoint links.

Six fixed commit identities were checked at recorded depths: two valid archives were fully extracted, MDrive source and real scenario payloads were inspected, CoLMDriver setup/evaluation entries were verified, and the Co-MTP and CMP codeload attempts were truncated and recorded as failures.
Verified one V2Xverse metadata row and the CoS-V2X model card with checkpoint/config names; no repository link alone was counted as an asset.
Drive links were not counted unless an inspectable sample, metadata record, checksum, or execution entry was independently verified.

ETSI TS 124 486 V18.4.0, the published form of 3GPP TS 24.486 Release 18, was inspected at clauses 6.13.1.2-6.13.1.6 and 6.13.2.2-6.13.2.6 for session-id-scoped update and termination requests, acknowledgements, notifications, and success/failure results.

searchAudit.canonicalization: Formal DOI or proceedings page is canonical when verified. The arXiv destination remains in links. Otherwise arXiv is canonical. Code, dataset, checkpoint, and project links are attached as assets rather than counted as separate papers.

priorDecisionFreeze.freezePolicy: A frozen topic may appear only as an explicit collision that rejects a newly phrased candidate; it cannot enter the shortlist without new primary natural evidence and a newly verified execution path.

limitations: Co-MTP and CMP fixed-commit codeload archives were truncated on two attempts each, so repository presence was not promoted to executable evidence.
V2X-Graph source archives contain Git LFS pointers for checkpoints; the pointer is evidence of a release contract, not proof that the weight payload was fetched in this audit.
MDrive is executable but CARLA and planner environments are heavy; only bounded scenario runs fit the two-week gate.
Several 2026 works are arXiv or project-page releases without formal proceedings at the cutoff date.
No private, gated, or Drive-only payload was treated as inspected data.

verifiedReferences.title: Co-MTP: A Cooperative Trajectory Prediction Framework with Multi-Temporal Fusion for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses cooperative history and future interaction; the paper explicitly conditions future fusion on ego planning information and other-agent intention predictions.

verifiedReferences.title: V2X-Seq: A Large-Scale Sequential Dataset for Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative Perception and Forecasting
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Introduces sequential cooperative perception and trajectory forecasting data; official code constructs cooperative identities using matching and multi-frame fusion rather than exposing a raw universal identity oracle.

verifiedReferences.title: V2XScenes: A Multiple Challenging Traffic Conditions Dataset for Large-Range Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative Perception
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides sequential perception/tracking data and unique track numbering over road sections; it does not release a cooperative forecasting or closed-loop planning task.

verifiedReferences.title: MDrive: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Cooperative Driving for End-to-End Multi-agent Systems
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Releases 225 closed-loop scenarios and reports that perception gains do not always improve planning and that negotiation can harm dense-traffic performance.

verifiedReferences.title: SwarmDrive: Semantic V2V Communication for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Reports compact intent distributions, event-triggered consensus, packet-loss and latency results, but evaluates a small prototype setting and does not expose verified code or checkpoints.

verifiedReferences.title: UrbanV2X: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal Dataset for Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative Navigation
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Releases 81 urban navigation sequences with sensor and route metadata; it is not an interactive multi-agent intent or closed-loop negotiation benchmark.

verifiedReferences.title: Defer to Plan: Adaptive Feature Fusion for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Reports closed-loop driving-score and infraction gains together with a route-completion decrease for one comparison, exposing a safety-efficiency tradeoff rather than a uniformly dominant result.

verifiedReferences.title: Select2Drive: Pragmatic Communications for Real-Time Collaborative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses predictive perception and area-of-importance communication and reports both offline-perception and closed-loop driving outcomes under bandwidth and pose constraints.

verifiedReferences.title: V2X-VLM: End-to-End V2X Cooperative Autonomous Driving Through Large Vision-Language Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Produces cooperative scene reasoning and planning outputs on DAIR-V2X-derived data, but the released evidence is open-loop rather than interactive closed-loop execution.

verifiedReferences.title: V2X-Graph: Learning to Predict Traffic Behaviors for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Releases cooperative trajectory-prediction code, V2X-Traj processing, sample-mode loaders, and checkpoint pointers, but evaluates forecasting rather than downstream closed-loop planning.

verifiedReferences.title: CMP: Cooperative Motion Prediction with Multi-Agent Communication
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Fuses multi-agent predictions and evaluates communication latency on OPV2V and V2V4Real; no closed-loop planner consequence is reported.

verifiedReferences.title: V2XPnP: Vehicle-to-Everything Spatio-Temporal Fusion for Multi-Agent Perception and Prediction
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses a unified spatiotemporal transformer for perception and prediction with one-step communication; prior local inspection found no complete trainer/evaluator/checkpoint release.

verifiedReferences.title: CoPAD: Cooperative Perception and Prediction for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Evaluates lightweight cooperative perception-prediction on DAIR-V2X-Seq with matching and tracking components, but no verified official code or checkpoint was found.

verifiedReferences.title: CoDriving: Toward Cooperative Autonomous Driving with V2X Communication
verifiedReferences.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides a CARLA/V2Xverse closed-loop cooperative driving baseline and a formal end-to-end planning reference.

verifiedReferences.title: UniV2X: End-to-End Autonomous Driving Through V2X Cooperation
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Unifies cooperative perception, prediction, and planning on logged V2X-Seq data; the planning evaluation is not interactive closed loop.

verifiedReferences.title: Coopernaut: End-to-End Driving with Cooperative Perception for Networked Vehicles
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: An executable CARLA cooperative-driving baseline with bandwidth and communication perturbation experiments.

verifiedReferences.title: CoLMDriver: LLM-based Negotiation Benefits Cooperative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Releases InterDrive and a CARLA negotiation-to-waypoint pipeline; reports an aggregate success-rate gain but does not test asymmetric intent revision delivery.

verifiedReferences.title: LangCoop: Collaborative Driving with Language
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Reports closed-loop CARLA results with language messages below 2 KB and a 96 percent bandwidth reduction, but no proposition-level acknowledgment or revocation protocol.

verifiedReferences.title: CoopReflect: Towards Natural Language Communication for Cooperative Autonomous Driving via Multi-Agent Learning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides six closed-loop negotiation scenarios, public message examples and quantitative outputs, and MQTT communication; the fixed code uses a latest-message age buffer without explicit semantic acknowledgment or revocation.

verifiedReferences.title: V2V-LLM: Vehicle-to-Vehicle Cooperative Autonomous Driving with Multi-Modal Large Language Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Releases multimodal V2V question-answer and planning-oriented outputs, not a verified interactive closed-loop control path.

verifiedReferences.title: Research Challenges and Progress in the End-to-End V2X Cooperative Autonomous Driving Competition
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Documents temporal perception and cooperative end-to-end planning tracks built on UniV2X and V2X-Seq-SPD and reports competition-level method results.

verifiedReferences.title: CooperScene: A Real-World Cooperative Autonomous Driving Dataset for Perception, Prediction, and Planning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Extends real-world cooperative data toward prediction and planning and advertises data and checkpoint releases; interactive closed-loop execution remains outside the logged-data release.

verifiedReferences.title: VLA4CoDrive: Vision-Language-Action Dataset for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides language-action supervision for cooperative driving but not an interactive message-loss protocol.

verifiedReferences.title: MORPH-U: Robust Cooperative Autonomous Driving under Unreliable V2X Communication
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Studies delay, drop, and forged-message conditions in CARLA with CAM/DENM-style messages; no verified official code/checkpoint entry was found.

verifiedReferences.title: V2X-ReaLO: An End-to-End V2X Cooperative Driving Framework with Real-World Deployment
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides real-world-oriented cooperative driving evidence but does not expose a compact public message-to-plan trace for this audit.

verifiedReferences.title: Safety-Aligned Cooperative 3D Detection for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Directly aligns cooperative perception with downstream safety outcomes, occupying generic perception-to-planning harm claims.

verifiedReferences.title: Hybrid Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative Autonomous Driving with Real-World Deployment
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides deployment-oriented vehicle-infrastructure evidence; the public record does not expose the per-message causal influence trace needed by an observability candidate.

verifiedReferences.title: System-Theoretic Framework for Intent Sharing in Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control
verifiedReferences.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Shows intent and status sharing are equivalent under reliable communication, while latest intent can reconstruct missing neighbor information under unreliable communication.

verifiedReferences.title: Do Open-Loop Metrics Predict Closed-Loop Driving? A Cross-Benchmark Correlation Study of NAVSIM and Bench2Drive
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Cross-references 15 methods across NAVSIM and Bench2Drive, obtains eight complete paired method records, and reports clear open-loop to closed-loop ranking inversions plus a safety-progress ordering mismatch. This directly occupies the matched-policy ranking-reversal question; changing to cooperative MDrive is benchmark transfer.

verifiedReferences.title: When Cooperation Should End: Maneuver Coordination Cancellation for Connected Automated Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Implements the complete Host/Remote maneuver-coordination cancellation state machine, Cancellation message, 100 ms retransmission, completion confirmation through the remote vehicle's next Intent, timeout, decision logic, and safe mobility recovery; reports shorter failed coordinations and more successful coordinations.

verifiedReferences.title: Importance of Intent-Sharing for V2X-based Maneuver Coordination
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Implements SAE-aligned maneuver coordination with Host/Remote states and Request, Response, Confirmation, and Intent messages. Intent messages broadcast the current planned trajectory when it changes significantly or after one second, and direct intent sharing is compared with kinematic trajectory prediction using successful and unsuccessful coordination outcomes.

verifiedReferences.title: 3GPP TS 24.486 Release 18: Vehicle-to-Everything Application Enabler Layer; Protocol Aspects; Stage 3
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Clauses 6.13.1 and 6.13.2 define session-id-scoped service update and termination requests, HTTP responses, acknowledgement elements, client notifications, and termination success/failure results. The standard therefore already supplies update, termination, and acknowledgement semantics at the V2X application-enabler session layer.

verifiedReferences.title: How to Stop Disagreeing and Start Cooperating in the Presence of Asymmetric Packet Loss
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Proves that deterministic cooperative-mode protocols necessarily have bounded disagreement periods under asymmetric loss and validates a mode-agreement protocol in NS-3.

verifiedReferences.title: AutoMCM: Maneuver Coordination Service with Abstracted Functions for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Implements seven maneuver-coordination messages with Autoware and OpenC2X and reports packet-loss robustness that depends on timeout settings.

verifiedReferences.title: Roadside-assisted Cooperative Planning using Future Path Sharing for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Implements future-path sharing with Autoware and LGSVL and reports intersection travel-time improvements for two vehicles.

verifiedReferences.title: Impact of Communication Loss on Model Predictive Control for Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Quantifies control consequences of communication loss in model-predictive cooperative driving, preventing packet-loss harm from being treated as a new generic phenomenon.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Motion Planning for Connected and Automated Vehicles with Intent Sharing
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Directly studies intent sharing in cooperative motion planning, occupying broad claims that intent exchange itself is missing.

verifiedReferences.title: AgentsCoDriver: Large Language Model Empowered Collaborative Driving with Lifelong Learning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses language-agent coordination for collaborative driving but does not provide a verified proposition-level loss and revocation experiment.

verifiedReferences.title: VIPS: Virtual Interactive Planning Simulation for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Releases pseudo-simulation tools, CoS-V2X code, a named checkpoint, and public comparisons between open-loop and interactive planning evaluation.

verifiedReferences.title: DriveX 2026 MDrive Multi-Agent Reasoning Challenge
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides the official competition entry for MDrive and confirms a cooperative closed-loop multi-agent evaluation track.

verifiedReferences.title: TalkingVehiclesGym Public Scenarios and Message Outputs
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Shows six scenario definitions, message examples, learned strategies, demonstrations, and quantitative result tables; these are lightweight public outputs rather than a bare repository link.

verifiedReferences.title: CoS-V2X Public Checkpoint and Configuration
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: The model card names latest.pth and sparsedrive_small_stage2_6cams_v2x_top100.py, providing a concrete checkpoint/config pair rather than a generic download link.

candidateLedger.title: Proposition-level intent revision under asymmetric partial delivery
candidateLedger.hypothesis: When one vehicle revises a semantic commitment such as yield-to-go while only a subset of peers receives the revision, latest-message timeout logic can make vehicles execute mutually inconsistent commitments even though every local message is syntactically valid.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: TalkingVehiclesGym uses latest-message age eviction without explicit intent acknowledgement or revocation, but the missing protocol function is already occupied. The VTC 2026 cancellation work implements a complete cancellation state machine, repeated Cancellation messages, remote completion confirmation, timeout, decision logic, and mobility recovery. The intent-sharing study represents intent as a changed planned trajectory inside a Host/Remote coordination state machine, and 3GPP TS 24.486 already defines session update and termination acknowledgements. Free-form language changes the encoding, not the coordination lifecycle or proposition-action identification object.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Revises or terminates an active maneuver commitment, propagates cancellation until remote confirmation or timeout, and changes the vehicles' executed mobility state.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: The candidate uses learned free-form messages instead of structured Cancellation and Intent messages; no proposition-action object was identified that cannot be represented by maneuver ID, coordination state, planned trajectory, and executed mobility.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.work: Importance of Intent-Sharing for V2X-based Maneuver Coordination
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Broadcasts changed planned trajectories as Intent messages and evaluates whether direct intent knowledge changes successful coordination outcomes.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Parsing a free-form commitment into the same planned-trajectory and coordination-state object is a representation change, not a new interaction function.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Defines session-id-scoped update and termination procedures with acknowledgement and client notification semantics.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: The standard is session-layer rather than maneuver-policy logic, but it removes novelty from generic update, termination, and acknowledgement machinery.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.work: How to Stop Disagreeing and Start Cooperating
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Bounds disagreement about cooperative versus autonomous operating mode under asymmetric loss.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Does not track the content lifecycle of a revisable semantic maneuver commitment or its executed trajectory.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Uses explicit maneuver states, retransmission, and timeout behavior under packet loss.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Does not test learned free-form intent revision or compare message belief against subsequent action in the same scenario.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Natural-language negotiation changes closed-loop decisions.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Published evaluations do not inject asymmetric delivery between an original intent and its revision, and do not score proposition-action consistency.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Uses latest intent to bridge unreliable communication.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Assumes structured dynamical intent in CACC, not conflicting semantic revisions in interactive maneuvers.

minimumEntry.entry: Add a deterministic per-receiver drop schedule around one original and one revised intent in TalkingVehiclesGym; log sent, received, active, and executed proposition state for both focal agents.
minimumEntry.requiredStack: CARLA, Mosquitto, official TalkingVehiclesGym; one GPU only for the released LLM policy, with a scripted policy as CPU control

twoWeekGoNoGo.compute: one GPU or CPU scripted control; three public scenarios; 30 fixed-seed episodes per cell
twoWeekGoNoGo.days: 2 setup, 2 protocol instrumentation, 3 intervention runs, 2 trajectory/proposition alignment, 2 asymmetric-loss controls, 2 analysis, 1 decision
twoWeekGoNoGo.go: At least one predeclared revision/drop cell produces a reproducible interval where agents hold incompatible active commitments and this interval predicts collision, emergency braking, deadlock, or route-delay change relative to both silent and acknowledged-revision controls.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGo: The intervention only ports structured cancellation, update, termination, or acknowledgement semantics into a learned/free-form planner, with no non-substitutable proposition-action identification target.
twoWeekGoNoGo.negativeResultConsequence: The candidate is stopped before execution because its positive result would validate an implementation transfer, not a new cooperative-driving conclusion.

candidateLedger.title: Matched-policy ranking reversal between offline and closed-loop cooperative driving
candidateLedger.hypothesis: For at least one fixed pair of cooperative policies evaluated on the same MDrive scenario subset, the offline ADE/FDE/AP or predicted-collision ordering reverses under closed-loop collision, route-completion, or driving-score outcomes.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: MDrive reports an open-loop evaluation gap, but arXiv:2605.00066 already compiles paired method results across NAVSIM and Bench2Drive and reports clear open-loop to closed-loop ranking inversions. Repeating the same paired-order test on cooperative MDrive changes the benchmark population, not the scientific question or conclusion.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.work: Do Open-Loop Metrics Predict Closed-Loop Driving?
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Pairs methods with open-loop and closed-loop results, measures rank association, identifies clear ranking inversions, and links the mismatch to safety-progress and compounding-error effects.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Using cooperative policies and MDrive instead of NAVSIM and Bench2Drive is benchmark transfer; the pairwise order-reversal object and conclusion are unchanged.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Defines open-loop and closed-loop metrics and reports broad perception-to-planning mismatch.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: The remaining test is narrower: identical policies, identical scenarios, pairwise order with uncertainty, and a result retained only if an actual order changes.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Contrasts open-loop with interactive pseudo-simulation evaluation.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Pseudo-simulation is not the same as CARLA closed-loop route and collision outcomes; it is a sensitivity baseline, not the target conclusion.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Asked whether perception gains reverse at planning level.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: That topic was rejected as broad and already evidenced. This candidate survives only as a concrete pairwise method-order claim with official scenario artifacts and an automatic kill if no order changes.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.sameFunction: Optimizes cooperative perception for downstream safety.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.remainingDifference: Does not establish which existing end-to-end method ordering reverses on a fixed MDrive scenario cohort.

minimumEntry.entry: Choose exactly two already-supported MDrive policy variants with available checkpoints, run the same 12-to-20 fixed scenarios, and pair official openloop_post_metrics outputs with closed-loop route/collision results.
minimumEntry.requiredStack: CARLA 0.9.12 and one supported MDrive planner environment on one GPU

twoWeekGoNoGo.compute: one GPU; exactly two policies; 12-to-20 scenarios; three fixed seeds where stochasticity exists
twoWeekGoNoGo.days: 3 setup, 2 smoke runs, 4 paired evaluation, 2 bootstrap/order analysis, 2 robustness checks, 1 decision
twoWeekGoNoGo.go: A predeclared policy pair has opposite offline and closed-loop order, with paired bootstrap support and a concrete collision, infraction, route-completion, or driving-score consequence.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGo: The paired ranking-inversion question and conclusion are already established; changing to cooperative MDrive is benchmark engineering rather than a new candidate.
twoWeekGoNoGo.negativeResultConsequence: A null or inversion would only characterize another benchmark population and would not create a new research blind spot.

conclusion.summary: No candidate survives without lowering the hard stops. The paired open-loop to closed-loop ranking-inversion question is directly covered by arXiv:2605.00066; moving it to cooperative MDrive is benchmark transfer. Semantic intent revision, acknowledgement, revocation, and cancellation are covered by the VTC cancellation implementation, the intent-sharing maneuver-coordination study, and 3GPP TS 24.486. Learned/free-form messaging changes representation but does not introduce a non-substitutable proposition-action identification object. All 15 candidates are mechanically rejected.

requiredRiskChecks.groundTruthEgoFutureOrOracle: Checked in Co-MTP and prior planning-conditioned forecast ledger; no new candidate retained because the exact audit remains frozen and non-executable.
requiredRiskChecks.globalIdentity: Checked in V2X-Seq/V2XScenes/V2X-Graph and prior identity ledger; no renamed identity candidate retained.
requiredRiskChecks.fullHistoryOneShotVisibility: Checked in V2XPnP/Co-MTP/V2X-Graph and prior causal-prefix ledgers; no candidate retained without a real checkpoint mutation.
requiredRiskChecks.splitLocationLeakage: Checked in V2X-Seq, V2XScenes, UrbanV2X, and prior split ledgers; rejected because no method ordering change or planner output was available.
requiredRiskChecks.openLoopClosedLoopSignReversal: Mechanically rejected after arXiv:2605.00066 verified paired method results with clear ranking inversions; cooperative MDrive would be benchmark transfer.
requiredRiskChecks.postLossIntentConsistency: Mechanically rejected after cancellation state-machine, changed planned-trajectory intent, and 3GPP session update/termination acknowledgement coverage left only a learned/free-form representation transfer.

conclusion.decisionRule: A candidate enters shortlist only when its exact function is not already occupied, at least one official asset or lightweight public output has been inspected beyond a link, the minimum entry is real, a CPU/single-GPU or small-sample two-week closure exists, and both positive and negative outcomes change a research or deployment conclusion.
